title: Prove scoped rational native-query lower bounds
body:
This adds scoped lower bounds for exact rational native-query words, including arbitrary dirty helper registers that return unchanged. The [proof guide](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/159dda696ee2004065d250da76d7d2b94a3e4f21/research/legacy-native-query-obstructions/README.md), [source manifest](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/159dda696ee2004065d250da76d7d2b94a3e4f21/research/legacy-native-query-obstructions/SOURCE-MANIFEST.json), and [independent agent review](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/159dda696ee2004065d250da76d7d2b94a3e4f21/research/legacy-native-query-obstructions/review/REVIEW.md) state the full contracts. The complete kappa calculation does not change.

The results rule out specific short native circuits:

- Rational monomial ADDRESS maps need at least `p*m` negative-determinant queries for the central `-I_m` endpoint on `p` productive roles. This count is sharp.
- Finite rational ADDRESS groups in three coordinates need at least `3*p` queries. This uses an explicit classical finite-reflection theorem dependency.
- Three productive roles with a plane `-I_2` endpoint need six queries, with all determinant signs allowed. Six coordinate reflections attain the bound.
- A subgroup character gives `p <= k+1` when exactly two queries are outside the subgroup and `k` inside queries have active character. A separate common-basis congruence theorem gives `q >= p*m`.

These proofs provide tests that a proposed shorter word must escape. They require exact formal group-algebra equality, rank-one query controls, and the stated ADDRESS alphabets. They do not exclude every dense rational eight-query word, initialized or discarded helper contracts, or general integer-multiplication algorithms. No new supplier, native tape implementation, or speedup is claimed.

The base is [cef4b52f2a59009865bf8eabde1be3f159063703](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/cef4b52f2a59009865bf8eabde1be3f159063703). [PR #521](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/521) supplies the native model at [a190fdb39f31647fc6f651625353710624627348](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a190fdb39f31647fc6f651625353710624627348/research/native-unipotent-fusion/PROOF.md). The [attribution qualification](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/159dda696ee2004065d250da76d7d2b94a3e4f21/research/legacy-native-query-obstructions/ATTRIBUTION-QUALIFICATION.md) credits Swapnil Jain's earlier dual-number methods and the prior mod-4 method. It also records the finite-reflection dependency. No literature-priority claim is made. Frozen source files and license notices are retained.

From the repository root, with Python 3 and the standard library, use a new output path:

```sh
python3 -B research/legacy-native-query-obstructions/verify.py --work /tmp/native-query-limits-replay
```

Expected final line:

```text
PASS_LEGACY_NATIVE_QUERY_OBSTRUCTIONS checks=5
```

All five exact checkers passed in the new independent replay. This includes all 576 products in the finite representation, 840 native factorizations, and 9,840 full group-algebra plane words. Endpoint, omitted-call, and noncommuting-order controls passed. The wrapper also rejected changed source bytes, optimized Python, and an existing output directory. Exact commands and results are in the [review receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/159dda696ee2004065d250da76d7d2b94a3e4f21/research/legacy-native-query-obstructions/review/REVIEW-RESULT.json). The general subgroup and congruence claims were checked as written proofs; finite examples do not prove their generality.

The older backup search over 82,320 positive-plane choices per form was not repeated. No selected-supplier cold replay, complete kappa computation, Lean proof, or hosted CI result is claimed. Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance was used for the work and packaging. Independent agent review is not human review. The dense rational escape and its implementation obligations remain open, as stated in the proof guide.
